items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: He certainly knew me because we had worked together in Luis Russell's orchestra at the Roseland

ctx.x: Eventually Connie closed the Inn and Russell went back to Roseland. I had been the featured soloist in the trumpet section and had some fine solos. Beezie and I had not yet started living together but we were sweethearts.

Russell had engaged a drummer singer to direct the band when we went in to the Roseland. His name was Tiny Bradshaw and he had been the drummer in the Blue Ribbon band. Tiny was a light-skinned, red-headed fellow who sang in the type of growl voice that was associated with Holy Roller preachers. Today its the way that most rock and roll singers sing. Tiny made a big hit at the Roseland, and the band was jumping.

Lucky Millender, who had been one of the directors of the Blue Ribbon orchestra, had an orchestra at the Harlem Opera House and was the regular house band. In June, Lucky sent one of his musicians to ask me if I would like to join his outfit for a job in France because Gus Akins suffered from some kind of sickness that did not permit him to travel overseas. I refused the offer because I was in love and did not want to leave New York, and at the same time I wanted to accept the offer. Everything was rosy for me…
